lines.text: Most of us picture a bank like a warehouse. You drop off $1,000, and they lend it to someone else.

post.yt_desc:
About 90% of the US money supply isn't paper cash: in August 2026, M2 hit a record $23.3 trillion, and cash and coins were only about $2.39 trillion of it. This video explains how banks actually create money: why the textbook money multiplier doesn't describe the system (US reserve requirements have been 0% since March 2020), how a single loan creates a brand new deposit, and why repaying a loan destroys money. A worked $30,000 car loan example shows the bank's books and the exact payment math, and we cover the real limits on lending: profit, capital rules, and the Fed's interest rate, plus the history from London goldsmiths to Silicon Valley Bank.
